_documentation: claude-secret-guard.allow.json — sanctioned-pattern allowlist for claude-secret-guard.js (BOW: tool.secretguard).
Format:
allowedPaths: array of { path, reason } objects (bare strings are rejected — every entry
needs a non-empty 'reason', same discipline as allowedPatterns below). 'path' is a glob
matched against staged file paths (forward-slash normalized, relative to repo root): '*'
matches within one path segment, '**' matches across segments (e.g. 'docs/**' allowlists
everything under docs/). A path match skips the WHOLE file for this hook — use it for
generated/reference files that legitimately contain hash-like or spec-prose content
(go.sum checksums, code.json/BOW-import GUIDs, docs spec prose), never as a way to
allowlist an actual source file with real secrets. A 'path' of exactly '**' or '*' is
rejected outright by the guard (over-broad — it would allowlist the entire staged tree);
scope every entry to a specific file or a bounded subtree.
allowedPatterns: array of { id, type, value, reason }. Every entry MUST include a non-empty
'reason' — the guard fails closed (denies the malformed-allowlist commit) if a reason is
missing, to keep this file self-documenting.
type 'exact'  — value is matched byte-for-byte against the extracted candidate string
(the connection string, the quoted literal, etc.) — never a substring
or fuzzy match (see AC-12: allowlisting the documented metro DB default
must not also allowlist a similar string with a different host/password).
type 'regex'  — value is a regex body (no leading/trailing slashes) that the guard
anchors itself ('^(?:value)$') and matches against the WHOLE candidate
string — again, never a bare substring search. Use for pattern CLASSES
like GUIDs/UUIDs, not for one-off literal strings (use 'exact' for those).
To add a new sanctioned pattern: prefer 'exact' for a single specific string (a known-safe
default credential, a fixture value); use 'regex' only for a genuine class of values that
are never secrets by construction (e.g. UUIDs). Always fill in 'reason' explaining WHY the
pattern is safe to ignore, not just what it matches.

allowedPaths.reason: Go module checksum file — entries are hashes by construction, not secrets.
Generated module registry (GR#3/GR#6) — carries GUIDs, which are identifiers, not secrets.
Generated BOW import staging file — carries the same GUIDs as code.json.
Spec/planning prose (acceptance criteria, master plan, this project's own docs) may quote example credentials, hashes, or GUIDs for illustration; not live secrets.

Generated replay-fixture sidecar headers (internal/harness/replay Save/Load). The high-entropy field is meta.SHA256, a content digest of the companion .ndjson.gz computed at write time — a checksum by construction, same category as go.sum. Scoped to the header sidecars only: fixture PAYLOADS are not allowlisted.

The secret guard's OWN regression suite. Its fixtures are, by construction, the things the guard must catch: seeded fake credentials, high-entropy strings, and GR#15 smells including the ALL-CAPS constant comparison that an earlier heuristic fix broke and this suite exists to pin. Scanning it produces guaranteed false positives forever, and blocking it means the guard prevents its own tests from being committed -- weakness pattern #5, a guard damaging what it protects. Scoped to this single file. Residual accepted knowingly: a REAL secret pasted into this file would not be flagged. Tolerable for a never-deployed test file whose diffs are reviewed as security work by definition; must not be extended to any other path. The Go-identifier suppression added for BUG-026 does not help here -- it is deliberately restricted to .go files, and this is JavaScript. Note for whoever edits this entry next: describing a smell in prose can itself trip the detector, so keep example patterns out of reason text rather than allowlisting this file.

The Part IV building catalogue (FEAT-010, 356 entries). Its ids are long lowercase snake_case names -- descriptive words joined by underscores -- which clear the entropy threshold on length alone despite having almost no real entropy per character. This is BUG-026's defect in a second dressing: BUG-026's fix suppresses candidates matching an identifier DECLARED in the same Go package, and these are data strings in JSON, so nothing declares them. Path-scoped rather than threshold-widened, because widening would blind the guard to genuine secrets of the same length. Residual accepted: a real credential added to this catalogue would not be flagged. Tracked as BUG-029 -- when the heuristic learns to recognise word-segmented lowercase identifiers, DELETE this entry rather than leaving it to rot.

Tests for the catalogue above. Same cause: they quote building ids (toxic_waste_plant, nuclear_..._half) and JSON field names (elecPerDay, foodPerDay, housingPerDay) as string literals, so BUG-026's same-package-declaration suppression does not reach them -- they are data keys, not declarations. Same residual and same removal condition as data/buildings.json: delete when BUG-029 lands.

allowedPatterns.reason: Documented metro MariaDB default (CLAUDE.md Environment section; claude-sync.js/claude-bow.js header docs): localhost, user root, empty password, db metro. Sanctioned local-dev default, not a live secret.
Same documented metro MariaDB default as metro-db-default-conn-127, using the 'localhost' hostname form instead of 127.0.0.1 (both appear across claude-sync.js/claude-bow.js/CLAUDE.md).
Canonical GUID/UUID form used throughout code.json and BOW item GUIDs (GR#6). These are identifiers, not secrets, and are high-entropy-looking by construction.

SEC-005 immutability tests use this literal as a deliberately invalid PhaseKind to prove a caller cannot inject a phase by mutating a returned copy. Descriptive test fixture, hyphenated English words, no secret material. Exact-matched so a similar-looking but different literal is not also allowlisted.

Correlation ID literal in the SEC-014 regression test, asserting the ORIGINAL Engine still works after a copy is rejected. Correlation IDs are a project-wide convention (GR#1); this one is descriptive English, not credential material.
Same shape as sec014-original-still-works, for the SEC-018 all-lock-sites regression test.
